channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: South Korean Won: Internationalisation roadmap supports won recovery – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Ma Tieying analyses South Korea’s new South Korean Won (KRW) internationalisation roadmap, unveiled by the Ministry of Finance and Economy, Bank of Korea and Financial Services Commission.

item.title: Australia unemployment rate set to steady at 4.4% in June, signaling strong job market
item.description: Australia will publish the June monthly employment report on Thursday at 01:30 GMT, and market participants expect a modest increase in job creation in the land Down Under.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar softens as oil and gold rally, ECB decision and Australian jobs loom
item.description: The US Dollar trades slightly lower on Wednesday as markets remain cautious amid escalating tensions surrounding Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. The US Dollar Index (DXY) slips toward 101.10, helping the Euro recover modestly, while most other major currency pairs remain relatively stable.

item.title: Philippine Peso: Under pressure from Oil surge – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that the Philippine central bank has intervened as higher Oil prices pressure Asian importers.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Downside risk persists against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/SGD is trading just above 1.29 after a quiet session, with momentum only tentatively firmer.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Breaks support trendline, eyes on 217.50
item.description: GBP/JPY holds firm on Wednesday, with the cross-pair trading above the 218.00 figure, as sellers seem to have the upper hand, after a break of a key support trendline, which could open the door for further losses. At the time of writing, the cross trades at 218.16, down 0.05%.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Growth shortfall feeds mild depreciation bias – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s FX research notes USD/CNY trading around 6.77, slightly lower on the day.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Swissy reclaims 0.81 as pair nears one-year high
item.description: USD/CHF registers solid gains on Wednesday, with buyers reclaiming the 0.8100 figure amid a trading session in which the Greenback loses ground against most G8 FX currencies but posts gains versus the safe-haven status of the Swiss Franc. The pair trades at 0.8146, up more than 0.20%.

item.title: Euro elevates ahead of ECB decision and Japanese inflation data
item.description: EUR/JPY trades marginally higher near the 186.20 area on Wednesday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains under pressure near multi-decade lows. The Euro (EUR) is relatively stable as investors avoid taking large positions ahead of the European Central Bank’s (ECB) monetary policy announcement.

item.title: Gold price breaks higher as US Dollar weakness fuels rally
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) surges over 1.50% on Wednesday, cracks a key resistance trendline and hits a new two-week high as the Greenback weakens. This Bullion price action comes despite rising tensions and hostilities between the US and Iran.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD struggles to build momentum above $60.00
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades with modest gains on Wednesday, supported by a slight pullback in the US Dollar (USD). However, the metal lacks strong upside momentum as traders weigh energy-driven inflation risks and their impact on the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest-rate outlook.

item.title: Euro gains against British Pound after mixed UK inflation report, ECB decision looms
item.description: EUR/GBP edges higher on Wednesday as a mixed UK inflation report weighs modestly on the British Pound (GBP). At the time of writing, the cross trades around 0.8533, extending its recovery after falling to its lowest level in more than a year earlier this month.

item.title: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rallies as escalation gets a price list
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades near 52,400 on Wednesday, up around 200 points and on track for a second consecutive daily gain, while the S&P 500 hugs the flatline and the NASDAQ Composite slips into the red.

item.title: British Pound steadies as cooler UK CPI meets Oil shock
item.description: The Pound Sterling holds firm during the North American session as UK inflation data dipped, easing pressure on the Bank of England to tackle higher prices, while attacks between the US and Iran don’t seem to be ending in the Middle East. The GBP/USD trades at 1.3377.

item.title: Canadian Dollar finds support from rising Oil prices, softer Greenback
item.description: USD/CAD edges lower on Wednesday as a mildly softer US Dollar (USD) and rising Oil prices help the Canadian Dollar (CAD) snap a two-day losing streak. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.4085, down 0.16% on the day.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar weakens as risk aversion overshadows hawkish RBNZ outlook
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5815 on Wednesday at the time of writing, down 0.16% on the day.

item.title: China: Fiscal execution to support growth – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economists Carol Liao and Shuang Ding argue that China’s July Politburo meeting will prioritise implementation of existing fiscal plans over new stimulus. They expect fiscal execution to accelerate in H2 after a marked slowdown following front-loaded Q1 spending.

item.title: Australian Dollar steadies ahead of Australian employment data
item.description: AUD/USD trades near 0.7000 on Wednesday, recovering from an intraday pullback but remaining marginally lower on the day. The pair briefly fell toward 0.6985 before rebounding, while the US Dollar Index (DXY) slipped toward 101.10, helping the Australian Dollar regain some ground.

item.title: Japanese Yen struggles near four-decade lows despite hawkish BoJ signals
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) gives up earlier gains on Wednesday, failing to capitalize on hawkish signals from the Bank of Japan (BoJ) and a softer US Dollar (USD) as Middle East tensions keep markets on edge.

item.title: Aluminium: Tariff tweaks seen as long-term policy – ING
item.description: ING analysts discuss changes to US Section 232 aluminium tariffs aimed at incentivizing domestic smelting investment. Qualifying projects can import at 25% instead of 50%, but ING stresses this is a long-term industrial policy with limited near-term impact.

item.title: Bank of Japan: Gradual tightening and external shocks – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s FX Strategy team reviews Bank of Japan policy, noting that the slow rate-hike pace reflects exceptional shocks such as tariffs, war and domestic political changes.

item.title: US Dollar: Range-bound gains and episodic strength – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect modest US Dollar (USD) strength in Q3 2026 as positioning has room to rebuild.

item.title: Euro struggles to extend gains as Iran war supports US Dollar
item.description: EUR/USD trades around 1.1415 at the time of writing on Wednesday, up 0.15% on the day, but its recovery remains limited after failing to break above 1.1420.

item.title: Gold hits two-week high as traders weigh Middle East risks, Fed outlook
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) climbs to a two-week high on Wednesday as bargain hunters step in near the $4,000 mark, while traders weigh Middle East risks and the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy outlook.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ hints at faster hikes – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that Bank of Japan (BoJ) officials are reported open to raising rates faster than economists expected as Japanese Yen (JPY) weakness lifts inflation risks.

item.title: Trump: 'US will bomb and destroy' Iranian bridges or power plants
item.description: US President Donald Trump issued a fresh warning to Iran on Wednesday, threatening strikes on the country’s infrastructure if Tehran targets vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Middle East tensions lift Oil as bulls test 100-day SMA
item.description: WTI extends its rebound on Wednesday as rising tensions in the Middle East disrupt Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $86.20 after reaching an intraday high of $87.83, its highest level since June 11.

item.title: United Kingdom: Core CPI resilience complicates BoE path – Nomura
item.description: Nomura strategists analyse the latest United Kingdom (UK) June inflation data, noting headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) fell to 2.6% as the Bank of England expected, but core and services inflation stayed sticky.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: NBH easing path shapes HUF prospects – ING
item.description: ING strategist Frantisek Taborsky reports the National Bank of Hungary (MNB) cut rates to 5.75% and confirmed dovish guidance, signaling further easing in August and possibly beyond. Markets have accepted renewed rate-cut pricing, and ING expects more dovish repricing.

item.title: Bank of England: Wait-and-see stance holds – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale economist Sam Cartwright analyzes June United Kingdom (UK) inflation, noting headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) at 2.6% year-on-year, below Bank of England (BoE) projections, with core inflation steady at 2.6%.
